video_title: Doug Christie details Kings’ mindset vs. beat-up Thunder | NBC Sports California

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on Keon Ellis's professionalism and fit with OKC
quotes.excerpt: there's a high level of professionalism he will fit in just perfectly. He's an incredible kid
quotes.quote: From what I understand about OKC, there's a high level of professionalism he will fit in just perfectly. He's an incredible kid, great work ethic, love him as a person. He'll fit.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie praises Keon Ellis for his professionalism and work ethic as he prepares to face the Thunder.

structured.context: Kings assistant coach Doug Christie discusses Keon Ellis's professionalism and how he will fit in with the Oklahoma City Thunder.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the diverse skill set of A.J. Lawson
quotes.excerpt: I think there's a lot of different players in him. He shoots the ball at all three levels
quotes.quote: I think there's a lot of different players in him. He shoots the ball at all three levels, he has runners, he can finish scoop shots, wrong-foot layups, shoots the free throw at a high percentage. Then the mid-range game is something that when he is looking for his game, he can go there and find it. He can shoot the three-ball, step up, off the dribble, step back. He's a special talent and we're being blessed to watch him, but also watch him evolve as a player.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie calls AJ Lawson a special talent and highlights his versatile scoring ability from all three levels.

structured.context: Doug Christie evaluates the diverse offensive skill set and development of A.J. Lawson.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on Keon Ellis's physicality and finishing ability
quotes.excerpt: Keon is bigger than you probably think and big shoulders, so if he's getting to the paint
quotes.quote: Keon is bigger than you probably think and big shoulders, so if he's getting to the paint, he doesn't see the runway. There's times that happens where people are there, that's when you want to play off to a tonic shoulder, pivot out of it and he has a really nice mid-range fallaway game, so he can use that, but also be able to see your teammates if the defense collapses.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie breaks down Keon Ellis's physical tools and his developing mid range game.

structured.context: Doug Christie breaks down the physical tools and playmaking abilities of Keon Ellis when he drives to the paint.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the high quality of the current rookie class
quotes.excerpt: there's a lot of really good players in this draft. Looking at Buzelis in Memphis
quotes.quote: There's a lot of really good players in this draft. Looking at Buzelis in Memphis, he fell into a really good system and he's just a really, really high level quality player. Dabossa watched him the other night in overtime and knocked down a big shot. There's a lot of really good players in this draft and it's going to be interesting to track them as they go along, but so far, a lot of talent.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie is impressed with the current rookie class, specifically noting the high level of play from Matas Buzelis.

structured.context: Doug Christie shares his observations on the quality of the current rookie class, specifically highlighting Matas Buzelis.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the Kings' team defense and player contributions
quotes.excerpt: their team defense is spectacular, that's what they rely on. If you turn the ball over
quotes.quote: I like the pace that Mitchell plays with. Mara on the interior is just huge. You see Hardenstein and what he can do in the floaters, the defense, pick-and-roll coverages. Their team defense is spectacular, that's what they rely on. If you turn the ball over, they are getting downhill extremely fast, but make no mistake about it, everything is coming through SGA and everyone gets to eat off of what he does.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the Thunder defense: Everything comes through Shai Gilgeous Alexander and everyone else eats off what he does.

structured.context: Doug Christie analyzes the defensive strengths of the Oklahoma City Thunder and the impact of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the Kings' internal focus despite opponent injuries
quotes.excerpt: we're looking at ourselves, trying to make sure that we're not turning the ball over
quotes.quote: As we continue to develop, you're not really looking at the opponent that way. We're looking at ourselves, trying to make sure that we're not turning the ball over, we're making sure that we're crashing, we're making sure that we're making second and third and multiple efforts on the defensive end, keeping a tight shell. All those little things that we need to focus on, the opponent is the opponent at this time.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie says the Kings are focused on their own internal development and defensive shell rather than the opponent's injury status.

structured.context: Doug Christie explains that the Kings are focusing on their own internal development and defensive habits rather than opponent injuries.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on Ben's return to practice and team impact
quotes.excerpt: everyone smiles and hugs him and is super excited to see him
quotes.quote: He's been around quite a bit actually. Everyone smiles and hugs him and is super excited to see him. As good as that probably is for Ben, it's as good as it is for us. That is the therapeutic piece of it, is seeing him, being able to have conversations with him, shake his hand, give him a hug, all those things I think they speak to him and watching him go through his process.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie shares the emotional impact of Ben's return to practice, calling it a therapeutic moment for the entire team.

structured.context: Doug Christie discusses the positive impact of Ben McLemore returning to the team's practice facility.
